existing_suite_pass_after: Tier 1: 650/650 (+1 skipped) | Tier 2: 12257 existing passed, 92 failed, 136 skipped, 7 errors (12506 collected, incl. 21 new)
_pass_after_note: NO REGRESSION, established by identity rather than by count. Tier 1: 671 passed + 1 skipped, 0 failed, in one run of all 10 frozen files plus the new one (671 - 21 new = 650 existing, matching the pre-change count exactly). Tier 2: the full broad net ran to completion on both trees. Raw failure counts move between runs (114 before, 92 after) because the failing tests are parallelism-sensitive server/sandbox/computer tests, so I adjudicated by identity: I extracted all 99 failing/erroring node ids and ran EXACTLY that set under identical conditions on both trees. Result: 65 failed / 34 passed on BOTH, with the sorted failure name sets identical in both directions (`comm` returns nothing either way) - zero failures introduced, zero fixed. Not one failure is in any test_llm_* module. NO existing test was modified, weakened, skipped or xfailed; the only test change in the patch is a new file.
api_cost_basis: Measured from recorded usage on every 200 response, priced at the published rates (gpt-6-astra $10/$50 per MTok; gpt-5.6-sol $5/$30 per MTok, the rate in gptme's own registry). Breakdown: 14 parameter-rejection probes returning HTTP 400 or 429 billed 0 tokens = $0.000; 5 tiny 200-probes (66 in / 51 out) = $0.003; live N=5 verification through gptme's own code path on gpt-6-astra incl. one smoke rep (7,602 in / 1,136 out) = $0.133; same on gpt-5.6-sol (7,219 in / 1,130 out) = $0.070. One request was measured before committing to any N=5 run (407 in / 56 out) and the run was sized from that measurement, not from a guess. A further 10 calls (the live M5 check, 5 reps on each model) returned schema-validation 400s and billed zero tokens.
errors_encountered: Background pytest runs killed twice by the harness at exit 144 (~10 min ceiling); worked around by splitting into per-file runs and using pytest-xdist -n 6/8.
`uv sync` does not install the poetry dev group; pytest and plugins installed explicitly into a venv (documented in the brief, cost ~5 min).
OpenAI flex tier returned HTTP 429 on gpt-5.6-sol while succeeding on gpt-6-astra, so the documented 50% saving could not be applied identically to both arms; ran standard tier on both.

`git stash push` refused to stash while an intent-to-add file was staged; abandoned a pre-change re-measure of two files rather than risk the working tree (the files pass post-change, so the measure was not needed).
Upshift's repair loop offered prompt text specific to its own bundled booking agent ('never claim nothing is available when search returned flights') to a terminal coding agent.
Live M5 check through gptme's --output-schema path returned HTTP 400 on BOTH gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-sol, 5/5 each - a pre-existing application defect (P7), not a migration regression.

problems_discovered.what: gptme validates GPTME_THINKING_EFFORT against one provider-wide set for every OpenAI model. gpt-6-astra rejects 'none' and 'minimal' with HTTP 400; 'none' is a working configuration on gpt-5.6-sol today, so an existing user config starts 400ing mid-conversation after the model switch. Sub-finding not in the supplied fact sheet: the accepted set is ENDPOINT-DEPENDENT - 'max' is accepted on /v1/responses and rejected on /v1/chat/completions.
problems_discovered.how_found: source reading, then confirmed by live API error

problems_discovered.what: _should_use_responses_api() honours GPTME_OPENAI_RESPONSES_API=0 and the LLM_PROXY path unconditionally. On gpt-6-astra with tools present that sends a request the model is documented to refuse, and the 400's own suggested escape hatch (reasoning_effort:'none') is itself rejected by this model - both confirmed live, in that order.
problems_discovered.how_found: source reading, then confirmed by live API error

problems_discovered.what: _maybe_apply_verbosity() and _make_responses_text_config() gate OPENAI_VERBOSITY on model.startswith('gpt-5'), so it is silently dropped on gpt-6-astra. Verified live that Astra ACCEPTS verbosity (HTTP 200 on chat completions and on responses as text.verbosity), i.e. the migration silently removes a working feature.
problems_discovered.how_found: source reading, then confirmed by live API call

problems_discovered.what: _prepare_messages_for_api() routes gpt-5* through _prep_o1 and every other reasoner through _prep_deepseek_reasoner. gpt-6-astra is a reasoner that does not match the 'gpt-5' prefix, so selecting it silently changes how the conversation is formatted on the Chat Completions path - a behavioural delta introduced by the migration itself rather than by the model.

Behavioural shift measured A/B at N=5: Astra chose `shell` with a printf redirect over gptme's dedicated `save` tool in 4/5 reps where gpt-5.6-sol chose `save` in 4/5; and on an open-ended edit task Astra used 7 assistant turns to the baseline's 6, spending them on self-verification. Both complete the task. Not patched - steering tool choice from a 4-case hand-written suite would be eval overfitting.
problems_discovered.how_found: tool signal (Upshift A/B at N=5, then my reading of the transcripts)

problems_discovered.what: NOT a migration regression, recorded for honesty: gptme never emits "strict": true for tool schemas on the Responses API (_tool_spec_to_responses_tool, openai_responses.py:174), although _spec2tool does on Chat Completions and the registry declares supports_strict_tools. Since Responses is the default path for every GPT-5+ OpenAI model, the flag is decorative for tools. Pre-existing and identical on both models.

fixes_attempted.fix: _MODEL_REASONING_EFFORTS (per-model, per-endpoint) + openai_efforts_for_model(); _resolve_reasoning_effort() gained a defaulted `endpoint` argument and raises a local ValueError naming the model, the supported levels and the migration guide's replacement ('Use \'low\' instead.'). Every supported list is quoted from the API's own 400 body.
fixes_attempted.why: Turns an HTTP 400 mid-conversation into an actionable local error. Defaulted argument keeps every existing caller and test untouched; two negative tests pin that unlisted models keep the full SDK-wide set.

fixes_attempted.fix: _MODELS_REQUIRING_RESPONSES_FOR_TOOLS + _should_use_responses_api(..., tools=None): with tools present on such a model the GPTME_OPENAI_RESPONSES_API opt-out is overridden with a warning; the proxy case warns clearly instead of failing cryptically.
fixes_attempted.why: The opt-out is a preference, and with tools present there is no working Chat Completions request to fall back to. Scoped by an explicit model list so no other model's behaviour changes.
One root cause, three symptoms; also stops the next GPT-6 model silently re-introducing them. Verified live that Astra accepts verbosity before enabling it.

The evidence is one case on a 4-case adapter I wrote myself. Writing system-prompt text to steer tool choice against my own eval suite is overfitting, and it would change behaviour for every gptme user on every model.

fixes_attempted.fix: None. Reported as an upstream issue candidate.
fixes_attempted.why: Pre-existing and identical on both models, so not a migration regression; making it live would change behaviour for gpt-5, 5.5 and 5.6 too. Out of scope for a migration patch.

fixes_attempted.fix: None. RECOMMENDED_MODELS['openai'] deliberately left at gpt-5.6-sol.
fixes_attempted.why: tests/test_llm_models.py::test_get_recommended_model hard-codes ('openai','gpt-5.6-sol'); flipping the default fails a frozen test, and modifying it is forbidden. M1-M5 are all phrased 'with the target model selected', so I made `gptme -m openai/gpt-6-astra` fully correct instead. Argued under 'disputed criteria' in RESULT.md.

unresolved_concerns: The behavioural A/B (P5) ran against my hand-written 4-case Upshift adapter, not against gptme itself. Running gptme's own gptme/eval/ harness at N=5 on both models was not affordable at Astra's $10/$50 with gptme's full tool-documentation system prompt. Estimated $15-40. NOT RUN. This is the largest remaining gap.

P7: gptme's --output-schema path returns HTTP 400 on every current OpenAI model because pydantic does not emit additionalProperties:false and gptme sends strict:true anyway. Pre-existing on both models, so out of scope for a migration patch, but it makes the frozen M5 criterion unsatisfiable at the pinned SHA. Deserves its own upstream issue.
P6: supports_strict_tools is a no-op for tool schemas on the Responses API (_tool_spec_to_responses_tool never emits strict). Pre-existing and identical on both models.
Astra costs 2x the baseline per token AND uses more turns, so the real cost delta for gptme users is larger than the price-list delta suggests.
Upshift's own cost accounting under-reports gpt-5.6-sol (prices it at $4/$20 against a published $5/$30), so its --max-cost-usd ceiling is looser than advertised on any model with a stale rate.

The 92-114 pre-existing Tier-2 failures are environmental on this machine (server port binding, sandbox, computer-use transport). They are unrelated to this migration but a maintainer should know the suite is not green here.

_adapter_note: Wall-clock minutes, corrected. ~11 min hand-writing the five adapter files (agent.json, system_prompt.txt distilled from gptme/prompts/templates.py, tools.json modelled on the strict-tool generation at llm_openai.py:2253-2261, a 150-line fake shell/filesystem backend.py, and 4 eval cases with checks and sim oracle plans); ~1 min on the free sim validation; ~2 min launching/babysitting the live run (which then ran ~12 min in the background while I worked on the patch); ~3 min reading four case transcripts to establish that 3 of its 4 reported signals were artifacts. `upshift capture` could NOT be used - hardcoded to Anthropic /v1/messages - which is exactly why the adapter had to be invented rather than recorded. This is 43% of the 40-minute wall clock.

_upshift_cost_note: `upshift cost` reports $1.3344. It prices gpt-5.6-sol at $4.00/$20.00 per MTok (src/upshift/pricing.py:56) where the published rate and gptme's own registry both carry $5.00/$30.00. Recomputing the baseline leg at $5/$30 with cached input at 10% gives $0.3472 rather than $0.2568 - Upshift under-reports that leg by $0.090, about 6.8% of the whole run. The gpt-6-astra legs agree exactly at $10/$50. BOTH figures recorded; the higher one used throughout. Not reconciled in the tool's favour.
